items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper explores an AI-powered framework designed to automate clinical audit narratives, leveraging large language models (LLMs) and natural language processing (NLP). The system employs fine-tuned GPT models, ICD-10-aware embeddings, and regulated prompt engineering to ensure legal compliance. This approach aims to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, and compliance of clinical documentation processes.</jats:p>
title: AI-Powered Generative Framework for Automated Clinical Audit Narratives: Regulated Prompt Engineering with LLMs and NLP

items.abstract: <jats:p>Enterprises rarely fail because their language model is incapable; they fail because the prompt pathway is opaque. We introduce prompt–centric observability (PCO), an operational discipline that treats inputs, routing, retrieval, templating, safety overlays, generation, and validation as first–class, measurable surfaces. PCO emits low–cardinality signals (coverage, support, freshness, p95, spend), binds drafts to the exact evidence spans they used, and routes decisions through a governed gate (release, rewrite, redact, escalate). We present a compact architecture, a minimal telemetry hook, and actionable controls for entitlements, privacy, and auditability. The goal is not a new leaderboard but predictable behavior under change: when data, policies, or templates shift, the system responds within guardrails and every outcome is replayable.</jats:p>
title: Prompt—Centric Observability: Debugging and Securing Generative AI Pipelines in Enterprise Deployments

items.abstract: <jats:p>AI agents are increasingly central to information systems, yet conceptual understanding of their engineering patterns remains fragmented. But developing robust and ethically aligned AI agents requires clear conceptual patterns guiding engineering practices. This study performs a structured conceptual analysis using existing prompt engineering patterns aiming to conceptually map prompting patterns found in Generative AI to Agentic AI, focusing on fundamental agent characteristics and critical AI risks and opportunities. Results indicate significant conceptual gaps in addressing ethical decision-making and transparency while adequately covering autonomy and basic collaboration. The patterns also underpin in a very tangible manner, an increased abstraction in prompting in agentic systems aligning with larger agent autonomy. The paper contributes a conceptual taxonomy that highlights areas needing further conceptual and empirical exploration, recommending future studies for empirical validation. It is also of value to practitioners who are commonly well-experienced in Generative AI prompting and aim to transition towards instructing and defining agents.</jats:p>
title: Agentic AI Prompt Engineering: Advancing Generative AI Patterns Conceptually
